solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps the lorry left paper off

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a big British truck

indicators.note: the paper's letters come off the word before it, leaving what remains

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a lorry drove away, leaving the newspaper behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes FT from LEFT, leaving LE. 'Perhaps the' defines by example: 'the' is the definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, so it is one instance of that part of speech.

clue.text: An orchestra's on top of that

parts.note: an gives the article a
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: An orchestra performs on top of something, perhaps a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition, besides, which is what 'on top of that' expresses.

clue.text: Clean up the fourth Mediterranean city

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to valet a car is to clean it thoroughly
IV is four in Roman numerals, as in a royal name like George IV

explanation.surface: A command to tidy up the fourth city on the Mediterranean coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses VALET to TELAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is Israel's second city, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Start to chop tree without a top

indicators.note: the start of the word chop is its first letter
without means the letter a is left out of the tree's name

parts.note: the rowan is the mountain ash tree

explanation.surface: Instructions to begin felling a tree that has no top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from ROWAN, leaving ROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown is the top of a head, a hill or a tree.

clue.text: English judge inspires fighter to leave country

indicators.note: inspires means breathes in, so the English judge takes the fighter inside

parts.note: to rate is to assess or judge
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: An English judge encourages a fighter pilot to move abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' pretends to mean encourages; here it means breathes in, so the fighter goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's homeland to settle in another nation.

clue.text: Current measure in Soho upset cleaner

indicators.note: the measure sits inside the rearranged London district's letters
upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the district's name is rearranged

parts.note: an amp measures electric current

explanation.surface: An electrician in Soho, a London district, knocks over a cleaning product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives SHOO; 'in' signals the insertion. Soho is a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a soap for washing hair or carpets, so it is a cleaning product.

clue.text: Like Simon or Herb

definitions.meaning: an old word for a medicinal herb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' could be a man's name next to Simon, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple describes the nursery-rhyme Simon and also names a single-plant herbal remedy.

clue.text: Collector opposed mine, right away

parts.note: anti means against, opposed

indicators.note: away signals the removal of the letter for right from the pit's name

parts.note: a quarry is an open pit mine

explanation.surface: A collector objected to a mine straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes one R from QUARRY, giving QUARY; it pretends to mean 'immediately'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiquary studies and collects antiques and relics of the past.

clue.text: Group punching glib country fan

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so the group goes inside the word for glib

parts.note: pat means glib, too ready, as in a pat answer
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A band hits a smooth-talking country-music lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punching' signals the insertion. 'country fan' suggests country music; it means a lover of one's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot loves and supports their nation, a fan of their homeland.

clue.text: Old one's in to raise work with puny margins for drug supplier

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the lifting verb

parts.note: to pump water is to raise it
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is read as 'is'
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: margins are the edges, so the outer letters of puny are taken

explanation.surface: An old man's in to lift weights and work on his weak edges for a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion and 'margins' the outer letters; 'with' is a link. 'to raise' is read as a verb for lifting liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: The opium poppy is the plant whose latex is the source of opium and heroin.

clue.text: Girl's back impeding soldier's view from premises

indicators.note: impeding means getting in the way, so the soldiers' letters stand in the middle of the girl's
back means the girl's name with its possessive is read backwards

parts.note: Molly is a girl's name, with the possessive S
a GI is an American soldier; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A woman's back blocks a soldier's view of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives SYLLOM and 'impeding' signals the insertion. 'premises' is the logician's sense: propositions an argument starts from.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllogism is a conclusion drawn from two premises in formal logic, a logical inference.

clue.text: African expresses disapproval with India

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval; he tuts
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa tuts at India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Squirm on TV and lie about dummy act

indicators.note: about signals that these letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer writhes on television and tells fibs about a stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SQUIRM ON TV LIE; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventriloquist makes a puppet, the dummy, appear to talk; that is the act.

clue.text: Random "Notes on a Small Island" seen in Circle Line

indicators.note: seen in means found within, so the notes and island go inside the ring and line

parts.note: a circle is shaped like O
C is a musical note; two of them give CC
Iona is a Hebridean island off Mull

explanation.surface: A copy of Bill Bryson's book 'Notes from a Small Island' spotted on the London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts CCASIONA between O and L; 'on' is a link. The Circle Line is a London Underground route.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasional means happening irregularly, now and then, rather than on any fixed pattern.

clue.text: Respect quartet I left in town

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the urban word

parts.note: a city is a large town
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A string quartet pays its respects to someone left behind in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion; 'quartet' is read as the Roman numeral four, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Civility is courteous behaviour, the politeness one shows when showing regard for others.

clue.text: Occupants of house provided in scruffy 28

indicators.note: in puts the condition word inside the rearranged letters
scruffy means untidy, so the letters of the cross-referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: 28 across is SLEEPER
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Members of a household, provided they are scruffy sleepers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' gives an anagram and 'in' the insertion. The House of Lords is Britain's upper chamber, where life peers sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Life peers are appointed members of the House of Lords whose titles are not inherited.

clue.text: Hide needlework display in Edinburgh

definitions.meaning: a design pricked into the skin (hide) with a needle
the Edinburgh Military ... is a famous annual display of military bands

explanation.surface: Someone conceals their embroidery at a show in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, conceal, but it is the noun: skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is both skin art made with needles and a military pageant with bands.

clue.text: They reflect action sure to curb traffic primarily

indicators.note: to curb means to restrain, so the legal action holds the letter inside

parts.note: a case is a legal action

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the initial letter of traffic is taken

parts.note: sure! means yes

explanation.surface: Action that is certain to slow down traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to curb' signals the insertion, making CATSE. Cat's-eyes are British road studs that reflect headlights.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's-eyes are reflective road studs that shine in headlights to mark lanes at night.

clue.text: Notice dispute off course

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a public notice
a rift is a break in relations, a dispute

explanation.surface: A notice about a quarrel has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat adrift has drifted from its intended route, so it is no longer on track.

clue.text: Element of watery discharge swamping part of UK

indicators.note: swamping means flooding over, so the discharge surrounds the region

parts.note: rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose
NI is Northern Ireland, a part of the UK

explanation.surface: Part of a watery discharge is flooding a region of the UK.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swamping' signals the insertion; 'of' is a link. 'Element' is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenium is a chemical element, a rare heavy metal with symbol Re.

clue.text: Youths with it claim Yankee title

indicators.note: claim means take in for oneself, so the young men hold the letter inside

parts.note: lads are youths
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Trendy young men lay claim to an American's honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claim' signals the insertion into the youths, making LADYS. 'with it' is one phrase meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladyship is a form of address and rank for a titled woman, as in 'Her Ladyship'.

clue.text: Lift remains of drink

definitions.meaning: a layer of leather in a shoe's heel, raising it
the liquor left in the bottom of a glass

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like a verb; it is a noun for a raised shoe layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heeltap names both a layer of leather built into a shoe heel and the dregs left in a glass.

clue.text: Flies before noon found in deep litter

parts.note: jets means flies, as in jets off abroad
a.m. is before noon

explanation.surface: Insects in the morning are discovered in thick bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in deep litter' is read as litter found in the deep: the sea. 'Deep litter' is also a poultry-bedding term.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard that ends up in the sea or washed ashore, marine rubbish.

clue.text: Popular paper by leaderless authority's beyond words

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
the Express is a British newspaper

indicators.note: the authoritative book loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: a bible is an authoritative book, as in 'the gardener's bible'; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A tabloid's account of an authority is said to be indescribable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the B from BIBLE, giving IBLE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexpressible cannot be put into language; it is indescribable.

clue.text: Bung joint in bloke's case

indicators.note: in puts the joint inside the outer letters of the man's word

parts.note: the case of the word bloke is its outer letters, B and E
a rib is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A cork is a joint in someone's suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: Bung is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is British slang for an illicit payment to secure favour.

clue.text: Run under superb service tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the run letter below the serve

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable tennis serve
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A tree service running under superb management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' wants to join 'tree' as a tree surgeon's firm; it belongs with 'superb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the genus of maples, so it names a kind of tree.

clue.text: Green where spring water comes from, seen travelling west

indicators.note: in an across clue, westward is right to left, so the brand is read backwards

parts.note: Evian is a French town famous for its bottled spring water

explanation.surface: A naive traveller heads west from a spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling west' reverses EVIAN; 'seen' is a link. Green means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone green is inexperienced and so innocent or unsophisticated.

clue.text: Old writers briefly endure dealing with technique

parts.note: styli are ancient pens for writing on wax tablets

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to stick something is to endure it, as in 'can't stick it'

explanation.surface: Classic authors briefly put up with matters of craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the K from STICK, leaving STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylistic means concerning style, the manner or technique of writing or art.

clue.text: Deposit, say, posh pharmacist in Hebridean stack

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the Scottish word for chimney

parts.note: lum is Scots for a chimney or chimney stack
U means upper-class, posh
MPS is Member of the Pharmaceutical Society

explanation.surface: A posh chemist in the Scottish Hebrides makes a deposit, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion. Lum is a Scots word for chimney; 'say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit, such as on a house, is often paid as one single payment of money.

clue.text: Coach line supporter

definitions.meaning: a beam that supports railway track

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a trainer, but it is a railway carriage; British 'sleepers' are what Americans call railroad ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from railways: an overnight carriage with berths and a beam under the rails.
